verdict.rationale: E2B documents running terminal commands inside the sandbox through the SDK `commands.run()` method, CLI exec (including background mode), and an interactive terminal. Package installation is supported but only implied: sandboxes have a real Debian toolchain and outbound internet by default, and templates can run commands at build time. missing for 10: an explicit documented example of installing packages at runtime (e.g., pip/apt inside a live sandbox), independent hands-on corroboration of arbitrary command execution.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run arbitrary shell commands and install packages inside the sandbox

citations.quote: You can run terminal commands inside the sandbox using the `commands.run()` method.
Use the `--background` flag to run a command in the background and return immediately.
You can create a sandbox and connect an interactive terminal to it.
your agent's code runs in an isolated Firecracker microVM instead of your server, with a real Debian toolchain
Every sandbox has outbound internet access by default.
You can define the base image, environment variables, files to copy, commands to run, and a start command
